# 委托

对视频主打的屏下摄像头（UDC）显示与成像折衷技术，做以本机为中心的深度研究

## 输入与工作方式

原问题亦见 QUERY.txt。源视频为 media/source.mp4，时间从片头0秒起，时长986.069秒，原声保留。
源页：https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1ua411J7VA

允许联网、自主选择研究方向、检索资料、安装依赖、编写脚本。没有额外的任务级工具次数、篇幅或研究条数限制。
不要访问本题隐藏评分文件、公开benchmark rubric、参考答案、先前交付或其他会话。

本环境不提供云端音视频理解或转写服务。已预装 FFmpeg/ffprobe、faster-whisper、PyAV、OpenCV、PyMuPDF、Pillow和Playwright；可以使用本地模型和工具自行感知音视频，也可安装其他依赖。

可自行抽帧：
`python toolkit/media.py frame --seconds 340 475 --out frames`

可截取单声道16kHz音频：
`python toolkit/media.py audio --start 320 --end 400 --out work/segment.wav`

可用本地faster-whisper转写（不调用云端模型）：
`python toolkit/media.py transcribe --start 320 --end 400 --model small --out work/transcript.json`

转写同时生成JSON和带绝对时间戳的TXT。`--model large-v3-turbo`使用已缓存的较大模型；`--media`可读取本运行目录内自行取得的其他视频或音频。模型在本地CPU运行，未提供GPU。工具只负责感知，输出可能有误，需回查原帧、原音和外部资料。

Python有PyMuPDF、Pillow、requests、Playwright，ffmpeg和Node在PATH。Playwright已安装Chromium，亦可用C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe。

## 报告交付

将完整报告交付至output/。使用随附的官方OmniDR报告渲染器；填写output/js/data.js（window.DATA = 严格JSON;），字段见output/js/data.schema.js，通用编写规范见REPORT_GUIDE.md。不要将字段示例当成事实或答案。
报告以视频为中心，综合外部研究；结论有来源和时间位置，相关帧和外部多模态证据可回查。引用使用[S#]并在research中记录实际打开的来源与本地证据。
output/index.html、js/data.js及其引用的本地素材均须存在，视频复制到output/media/source.mp4。保留模板的index.html、styles.css、js/app.js和js/link.js，可自选已有主题。布局和交互已提供，主要工作是研究和证据组织。
TOOLS_USED.md只记录真实工具、来源和实测检查。模板中的review/validate_omnidr_report等MCP服务本环境未安装；可用node toolkit/validate_data.mjs output/js/data.js，并用Playwright实际检查页面播放、时间跳转、引用和图片。
不必额外交付research.json或复现内部研究流程。不要修改源视频或本任务文件。完成后正常总结。

events.body:
# Report data and delivery

`prepare_omnidr_report` creates a portable directory with browser-ready source media,
the existing OmniDR renderer, its data schema and an empty draft. It refuses to overwrite
an existing directory. Resume by reading the files, not by initializing again.

```text
report/
  index.html
  styles.css
  js/{app.js,link.js,data.schema.js,data.js}
  media/source.mp4
  img/                       segment frames
  anchors/                   object and citation crops
  _assets/{videos,images,docs}/
  _work/                     reading manifests, transcripts, notes and research-review.json
  omnidr-project.json        source fingerprint and timeline
  TOOLS_USED.md              provenance and review notes
```

Serialize `window.DATA = <JSON>;` with `json.dumps`/`JSON.stringify`. No executable JS,
comments, templates, functions or trailing commas. `js/data.schema.js` is a reference;
do not copy it over data.js. Edit data/evidence only; retain the renderer.

Essential shape:

- `meta`: theme `t01`–`t20`, subject category and language `zh` or `en`.
- `video`: title, `media/source.mp4`, positive source duration and optional local poster.
- `summary`: subject-facing overview.
- `segments`: source-absolute `start/end`, title, keyframe, ordered caption blocks,
  source IDs and optional segment-level insights.
- `anchors`: planning reasons tied to real segment IDs.
- `research`: opened sources with IDs, canonical URLs, findings, `anchorId`, and local
  `media` paths and `publisher`. Video entries use `perception` for the complete
  reading.json manifest; primary text sources have `primary: true`.
- `insights`: source-backed comparisons, causes, context and dated corrections. Both
  top-level and segment-level comparisons/corrections require two sources and evidence.

Use inline `[S#]` citations. Caption blocks support text, image, flow, mindmap and static
SVG; insight comparison tables use the schema's table structure. Explain the subject
on the page. Keep workflow steps, research quotas and tool diagnostics in `TOOLS_USED.md`.

## Illustrated notes and built-in diagrams

Use a representative frame inside each segment's interval where permitted. Use each
image once, as a keyframe or caption block; prefer a caption block for explicit frame
time and credits. The renderer suppresses repeated images. Use the extractor's returned
**actual timestamp**, since sharp-frame selection may move away from the requested
instant. Put that time in the caption, e.g. `02:35 — the observed control setting`.
Inspect the crop/frame you will publish. A missing or refused visual interval remains
a disclosed gap; do not move an unrelated earlier image into it to fill the layout.

Interleave prose, frames and object crops. Reconcile saved image assets with their
actual report positions; an internal anchor reference does not display a crop.
Keep review-only frames and superseded assets with provenance under `_work/`, not
delivery image folders. Preserve useful evidence; never delete it to improve a count.
Identify external illustrations with source citations. Give segments content-specific
titles, including opening/closing material, without inventing content to expand a title.

Built-in `caption` blocks:

```json
{"type":"flow","title":"How the outcome follows","steps":["Observed condition [S1]","Supported mechanism [S2]","Practical consequence [S1][S2]"]}
```

```json
{"type":"mindmap","root":"Decision criteria","branches":[{"label":"Performance","items":["Relevant measured condition [S1]"]},{"label":"Constraints","items":["Documented limitation [S2]"]}]}
```

Replace the example content with actual findings and existing source IDs. Use a flow
for a causal chain or decision sequence, a mind map for genuinely branching factors,
and a comparison table for parallel alternatives. A structured block should clarify
the subject, not diagram the research workflow. SVG charts are also supported; supply
static, self-contained markup with cited data in a `type: "svg"` block.
Use image blocks for inspected raster frames/photos. Do not invent data or require
a separate diagram service. Read the generated schema for the table format.

`authoring_diagnostics.presentation` lists unplaced images, generic titles, repeated/
misaligned frames and missing caption times/illustrations without reading pixels. A zero
`structured_diagram_blocks` count suggests considering a useful diagram, not filler.

All media and evidence paths must stay inside the report and refer to regular local
files. Copy artifacts rather than linking to temporary files or private source folders.
Exclude authentication data, cookie files, environment files and model weights.

Run `validate_omnidr_report(stage="structure")` after each substantial authoring pass;
run `stage="delivery"` before delivery using the ledger in [review.md](review.md). It
rejects incomplete drafts, invalid citations and anchors, missing media, unbacked
comparison/correction quotes, altered renderer files, and accidental credential files.
A structural pass returns `structure_valid` and never marks `delivery_ready`. A delivery
pass also checks the research requirements and recorded review, but is not a claim of
independently verified research quality.

Use `omnidr_screenshot`, then inspect the image. Test playback, seeking both ways,
citations, images and language/theme in both panes. Run custom Playwright checks
with the Python interpreter used by the MCP server. Open the absolute `index.html` file URI.
HTTP needs Range/206; plain `python -m http.server` can break seeking.
Record measured play/seek results; exit 0 alone is not a pass. Expand details
before clicking a visible citation. Page checks do not establish factual support.

--- data.schema.js ---
/* OmniDR report field reference. This commented object is DOCUMENTATION, not data.js.
 * Write data.js with a JSON serializer: window.DATA = <strict JSON>;
 * Renderer inputs contain no functions or executable expressions.
 * Times refer to the original source. Media/evidence paths stay inside the report.
 * Fill fields from observations and saved sources, not the illustrative values here.
 */
window.OMNIDR_SCHEMA_EXAMPLE = {
  meta: { theme: "t05", category: "Subject category", lang: "en" },
  summary: "The source and the externally supported finding [S1].",
  video: { src: "media/source.mp4", title: "Video title", duration: 120, poster: "img/poster.jpg" },
  segments: [
    {
      id: "seg1", start: 0, end: 120, title: "Semantic segment title",
      keyframe: "img/seg1-00m30s.jpg",
      caption: [
        { type: "text", text: "Observed visual and spoken content. External claims cite [S1]." },
        { type: "image", src: "anchors/A1-detail.jpg", cap: "What this source crop shows." },
        { type: "flow", title: "Process", steps: ["Step one", "Step two"] },
        { type: "mindmap", root: "Topic", branches: [{ label: "Branch", items: ["Detail"] }] },
        { type: "svg", svg: "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" viewBox=\"0 0 100 100\"><circle cx=\"50\" cy=\"50\" r=\"20\"/></svg>" }
      ],
      sources: ["S1"],
      insights: [] // Same insight shapes and evidence requirements as the top-level array.
    }
  ],
  anchors: [
    {
      id: "A1", label: "Research question", category: "comparison",
      why: "Why external evidence would help the viewer.", segmentIds: ["seg1"],
      frame: "anchors/A1-detail.jpg" // Optional inspected source crop.
    }
  ],
  // Categories: background, more support, comparison, commentary, related material, timeliness.
  // Chinese equivalents: 背景知识, 更多支撑, 类似产品·事件对比, 网络观点评论, 相似资料, 时效纠偏.
  research: [
    {
      id: "S1", type: "web", title: "Opened source title", url: "https://example.org/article",
      summary: "The finding actually read from this source.", anchorId: "A1",
      publisher: "Independent author or publisher", primary: true,
      media: "_assets/docs/S1.html" // Required saved evidence; thumb is an optional local image.
    },
    {
      id: "S2", type: "video", title: "Watched related video", url: "https://example.org/watch",
      summary: "Finding grounded in inspected visual and audio ranges.", anchorId: "A1",
      publisher: "Independent video creator",
      media: "_assets/videos/S2.mp4", perception: "_work/S2/reading.json"
    }
  ],
  // Source types: web, image, video, report. A PDF uses type report and a local PDF media path.
  insights: [
    {
      kind: "compare", title: "A supported comparison",
      table: { cols: ["Dimension", "Source video", "External evidence"], rows: [["Dimension A", "Value", "Value"]] },
      body: "The comparison and its practical implication [S1][S2].", sources: ["S1", "S2"],
      evidence: [
        { srcId: "S1", quote: "A verbatim passage of at least twenty characters from the saved source.", local: "_assets/docs/S1.html" },
        { srcId: "S2", quote: "A faithful transcript passage supporting the compared statement.", local: "_assets/docs/S2-transcript.txt" }
      ]
    },
    { kind: "cause", title: "Explanation", body: "A source-backed explanation [S1].", sources: ["S1"] },
    { kind: "context", title: "Background", body: "Useful background [S1].", sources: ["S1"] }
  ]
};
/* Timeliness insights use kind: "timeliness", title, videoClaim, currentFact,
 * sources and evidence. Include the as-of date and preserve units. Like compare,
 * they require at least two independently produced sources and saved quoted evidence
 * for EVERY cited source, at both report and segment level. Use faithful text extracts
 * for binary PDFs. Mechanical quote matching does not establish the claim's truth.
 */

/* Delivery also requires _work/research-review.json: full source/video readings,
 * primary-reader notes, inspected used crops, current per-claim reviews and browser
 * checks. See the Skill review reference. A structural pass is not delivery-ready. */

"""Local-only media helpers: FFmpeg frames/audio and faster-whisper."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import wave

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MODELS = {
    "small": "[user]/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Systran--faster-whisper-small/snapshots/536b0662742c02347bc0e980a01041f333bce120",
    "large-v3-turbo": "[user]/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--mobiuslabsgmbh--faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo/snapshots/0a363e9161cbc7ed1431c9597a8ceaf0c4f78fcf",
}


def media_path(value):
    path = (ROOT / value).resolve()
    if not path.is_relative_to(ROOT.resolve()) or not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError("Media must be a file inside this run")
    return path


def duration(path):
    raw = subprocess.check_output([
        "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(path),
    ], text=True)
    return float(raw.strip())


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True)
    frames = sub.add_parser("frame")
    frames.add_argument("--seconds", nargs="+", type=float, required=True)
    frames.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    frames.add_argument("--media", default="media/source.mp4")
    audio = sub.add_parser("audio")
    audio.add_argument("--start", type=float, default=0)
    audio.add_argument("--end", type=float)
    audio.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    audio.add_argument("--media", default="media/source.mp4")
    transcript = sub.add_parser("transcribe")
    transcript.add_argument("--start", type=float, default=0)
    transcript.add_argument("--end", type=float)
    transcript.add_argument("--model", choices=sorted(MODELS), default="small")
    transcript.add_argument("--language", default="zh")
    transcript.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    transcript.add_argument("--media", default="media/source.mp4")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    source = media_path(args.media)
    total = duration(source)
    if args.action == "frame":
        args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for timestamp in args.seconds:
            if not 0 <= timestamp < total:
                raise ValueError("Time outside video")
            target = args.out / f"frame-{timestamp:09.3f}.png"
            subprocess.run([
                "ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", str(timestamp),
                "-i", str(source), "-frames:v", "1", str(target),
            ], check=True)
            print(str(target))
        return
    end = total if args.end is None else args.end
    if not 0 <= args.start < end <= total + 0.01:
        raise ValueError("Use a valid time range inside the media")
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if args.action == "audio":
        subprocess.run([
            "ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", str(args.start),
            "-to", str(end), "-i", str(source), "-vn", "-ac", "1",
            "-ar", "16000", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", str(args.out),
        ], check=True)
        print(str(args.out))
        return
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    clip = args.out.parent / (args.out.stem + "-clip.wav")
    try:
        subprocess.run([
            "ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", str(args.start),
            "-to", str(end), "-i", str(source), "-vn", "-ac", "1",
            "-ar", "16000", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", str(clip),
        ], check=True)
        model = WhisperModel(
            MODELS[args.model], device="cpu", compute_type="int8",
            cpu_threads=4, local_files_only=True,
        )
        with wave.open(str(clip), "rb") as stream:
            assert stream.getnchannels() == 1 and stream.getsampwidth() == 2
            audio = np.frombuffer(
                stream.readframes(stream.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16,
            ).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
        segments, info = model.transcribe(
            audio, language=args.language, beam_size=5, vad_filter=True,
        )
        rows = [{
            "start": round(args.start + segment.start, 3),
            "end": round(args.start + segment.end, 3),
            "text": segment.text.strip(),
        } for segment in segments]
        result = {
            "media": args.media,
            "requested_range": [args.start, end],
            "model": args.model,
            "engine": "faster-whisper/local CPU; no cloud media service",
            "language": info.language,
            "language_probability": info.language_probability,
            "segments": rows,
        }
        args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        args.out.with_suffix(".txt").write_text(
            "\n".join(f"[{r['start']:.3f} --> {r['end']:.3f}] {r['text']}" for r in rows) + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
    finally:
        clip.unlink(missing_ok=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# 委托

对视频主打的屏下摄像头（UDC）显示与成像折衷技术，做以本机为中心的深度研究

## 输入与工作方式

原问题亦见 QUERY.txt。源视频为 media/source.mp4，时间从片头0秒起，时长986.069秒，原声保留。
源页：https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1ua411J7VA

允许联网、自主选择研究方向、检索资料、安装依赖、编写脚本。没有额外的任务级工具次数、篇幅或研究条数限制。
不要访问本题隐藏评分文件、公开benchmark rubric、参考答案、先前交付或其他会话。

本环境不提供云端音视频理解或转写服务。已预装 FFmpeg/ffprobe、faster-whisper、PyAV、OpenCV、PyMuPDF、Pillow和Playwright；可以使用本地模型和工具自行感知音视频，也可安装其他依赖。

可自行抽帧：
`python toolkit/media.py frame --seconds 340 475 --out frames`

可截取单声道16kHz音频：
`python toolkit/media.py audio --start 320 --end 400 --out work/segment.wav`

可用本地faster-whisper转写（不调用云端模型）：
`python toolkit/media.py transcribe --start 320 --end 400 --model small --out work/transcript.json`

转写同时生成JSON和带绝对时间戳的TXT。`--model large-v3-turbo`使用已缓存的较大模型；`--media`可读取本运行目录内自行取得的其他视频或音频。模型在本地CPU运行，未提供GPU。工具只负责感知，输出可能有误，需回查原帧、原音和外部资料。

Python有PyMuPDF、Pillow、requests、Playwright，ffmpeg和Node在PATH。Playwright已安装Chromium，亦可用C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe。

## 报告交付

将完整报告交付至output/。使用随附的官方OmniDR报告渲染器；填写output/js/data.js（window.DATA = 严格JSON;），字段见output/js/data.schema.js，通用编写规范见REPORT_GUIDE.md。不要将字段示例当成事实或答案。
报告以视频为中心，综合外部研究；结论有来源和时间位置，相关帧和外部多模态证据可回查。引用使用[S#]并在research中记录实际打开的来源与本地证据。
output/index.html、js/data.js及其引用的本地素材均须存在，视频复制到output/media/source.mp4。保留模板的index.html、styles.css、js/app.js和js/link.js，可自选已有主题。布局和交互已提供，主要工作是研究和证据组织。
TOOLS_USED.md只记录真实工具、来源和实测检查。模板中的review/validate_omnidr_report等MCP服务本环境未安装；可用node toolkit/validate_data.mjs output/js/data.js，并用Playwright实际检查页面播放、时间跳转、引用和图片。
不必额外交付research.json或复现内部研究流程。不要修改源视频或本任务文件。完成后正常总结。

events.body:
# Report data and delivery

`prepare_omnidr_report` creates a portable directory with browser-ready source media,
the existing OmniDR renderer, its data schema and an empty draft. It refuses to overwrite
an existing directory. Resume by reading the files, not by initializing again.

```text
report/
  index.html
  styles.css
  js/{app.js,link.js,data.schema.js,data.js}
  media/source.mp4
  img/                       segment frames
  anchors/                   object and citation crops
  _assets/{videos,images,docs}/
  _work/                     reading manifests, transcripts, notes and research-review.json
  omnidr-project.json        source fingerprint and timeline
  TOOLS_USED.md              provenance and review notes
```

Serialize `window.DATA = <JSON>;` with `json.dumps`/`JSON.stringify`. No executable JS,
comments, templates, functions or trailing commas. `js/data.schema.js` is a reference;
do not copy it over data.js. Edit data/evidence only; retain the renderer.

Essential shape:

- `meta`: theme `t01`–`t20`, subject category and language `zh` or `en`.
- `video`: title, `media/source.mp4`, positive source duration and optional local poster.
- `summary`: subject-facing overview.
- `segments`: source-absolute `start/end`, title, keyframe, ordered caption blocks,
  source IDs and optional segment-level insights.
- `anchors`: planning reasons tied to real segment IDs.
- `research`: opened sources with IDs, canonical URLs, findings, `anchorId`, and local
  `media` paths and `publisher`. Video entries use `perception` for the complete
  reading.json manifest; primary text sources have `primary: true`.
- `insights`: source-backed comparisons, causes, context and dated corrections. Both
  top-level and segment-level comparisons/corrections require two sources and evidence.

Use inline `[S#]` citations. Caption blocks support text, image, flow, mindmap and static
SVG; insight comparison tables use the schema's table structure. Explain the subject
on the page. Keep workflow steps, research quotas and tool diagnostics in `TOOLS_USED.md`.

## Illustrated notes and built-in diagrams

Use a representative frame inside each segment's interval where permitted. Use each
image once, as a keyframe or caption block; prefer a caption block for explicit frame
time and credits. The renderer suppresses repeated images. Use the extractor's returned
**actual timestamp**, since sharp-frame selection may move away from the requested
instant. Put that time in the caption, e.g. `02:35 — the observed control setting`.
Inspect the crop/frame you will publish. A missing or refused visual interval remains
a disclosed gap; do not move an unrelated earlier image into it to fill the layout.

Interleave prose, frames and object crops. Reconcile saved image assets with their
actual report positions; an internal anchor reference does not display a crop.
Keep review-only frames and superseded assets with provenance under `_work/`, not
delivery image folders. Preserve useful evidence; never delete it to improve a count.
Identify external illustrations with source citations. Give segments content-specific
titles, including opening/closing material, without inventing content to expand a title.

Built-in `caption` blocks:

```json
{"type":"flow","title":"How the outcome follows","steps":["Observed condition [S1]","Supported mechanism [S2]","Practical consequence [S1][S2]"]}
```

```json
{"type":"mindmap","root":"Decision criteria","branches":[{"label":"Performance","items":["Relevant measured condition [S1]"]},{"label":"Constraints","items":["Documented limitation [S2]"]}]}
```

Replace the example content with actual findings and existing source IDs. Use a flow
for a causal chain or decision sequence, a mind map for genuinely branching factors,
and a comparison table for parallel alternatives. A structured block should clarify
the subject, not diagram the research workflow. SVG charts are also supported; supply
static, self-contained markup with cited data in a `type: "svg"` block.
Use image blocks for inspected raster frames/photos. Do not invent data or require
a separate diagram service. Read the generated schema for the table format.

`authoring_diagnostics.presentation` lists unplaced images, generic titles, repeated/
misaligned frames and missing caption times/illustrations without reading pixels. A zero
`structured_diagram_blocks` count suggests considering a useful diagram, not filler.

All media and evidence paths must stay inside the report and refer to regular local
files. Copy artifacts rather than linking to temporary files or private source folders.
Exclude authentication data, cookie files, environment files and model weights.

Run `validate_omnidr_report(stage="structure")` after each substantial authoring pass;
run `stage="delivery"` before delivery using the ledger in [review.md](review.md). It
rejects incomplete drafts, invalid citations and anchors, missing media, unbacked
comparison/correction quotes, altered renderer files, and accidental credential files.
A structural pass returns `structure_valid` and never marks `delivery_ready`. A delivery
pass also checks the research requirements and recorded review, but is not a claim of
independently verified research quality.

Use `omnidr_screenshot`, then inspect the image. Test playback, seeking both ways,
citations, images and language/theme in both panes. Run custom Playwright checks
with the Python interpreter used by the MCP server. Open the absolute `index.html` file URI.
HTTP needs Range/206; plain `python -m http.server` can break seeking.
Record measured play/seek results; exit 0 alone is not a pass. Expand details
before clicking a visible citation. Page checks do not establish factual support.

16: 17: 22: 26: 29: Camera in Display | Applied Sciences | Microsoft 32: 44: display: block; 232: Microsoft Learn 272: display: none; 304: Camera in display 307: Machine learning and embedded cameras make possible a new class of more natural videoconferencing devices 314: 321: The idea of embedding cameras in a display is not new.  From the earliest days of videoconferencing it was recognized that the separation of the camera and the display meant the system could not convey gaze awareness 325: A second challenge has emerged more recently.  The desire to maximize screen size on small devices such as cell phones leaves little room outside the display to locate a camera. 328: Placing cameras behind the screen could solve these problems, but doing so tends to degrade the image.  Diffraction from the screen’s pixel structure can blur the image, reduce contrast, reduce usable light 329: levels, and even obstruct some image content entirely, in ways that are dependent on the device’s display-pixel design. 335: In this project we investigate how machine learning can help overcome some of the image degradation problems associated with placing cameras behind the display, and can help frame remote conversations in 343: Locating the camera above the display results in a vantage point that’s different from a face-to-face conversation, especially with large displays, which can create a sense of looking down on the person speaking. 346: Worse, the distance between the camera and the display mean that the participants will not experience a sense of eye contact.  If I look directly into your eyes on the screen, you will see me apparently gazing below 347: your face.  Conversely, if I look directly into the camera to give you a sense that I am looking into your eyes, I’m no longer in fact able to see your eyes, and I may miss subtle non-verbal feedback cues. 355: 356: 359: 360: 368: Relocating the camera to the point on the screen where the remote participant’s face appears would achieve a natural perspective and a sense of eye contact. 372:

The Diffraction Difficulty

375: With transparent OLED displays (T-OLED), we can position a camera behind the screen, potentially solving the perspective problem.  But because the screen is not fully transparent, looking through it degrades image quality by introducing diffraction and noise. 383: 387: 388: 393: Pixel structure affects diffraction.  In this example, the screen has a long, thin rectangle to view through: 397: 398: 407: 408: 411: 412: 428: 432: 435: 443: 447: 450: 458: 462: 465: 471: The ability to position cameras in the display and still maintain good image quality provides an effective solution to the perennial problems of gaze awareness and perspective. 478: 489: Such factors could be applied to the virtual environment of a remote conversation by adjusting the speaker’s position and size on the display. 500: 510: 513: 525: Having identified the speaker in the remote view, we can scale the incoming video so that the remote participant appears in a lifelike size on the local display. 530: 534: 546: 554: display other information, such as presentation slides or video that the speaker is talking about. 561: Human interaction in videoconferences can be made more natural by correcting gaze, scale, and position by using convolutional neural network segmentation together with cameras embedded in a partially transparent display.  The diffraction and noise resulting from placing the camera behind the screen can be effectively removed using U-net neural network.  Segmentation of live video also makes it possible to combine the speaker with a choice of background content. 564: Neural networks combined with T-OLED displays create a new class of videoconference devices. 571:

211-

为大场面而生 终极直板旗舰中兴Axon 40 Ultra正式发布

212-

2022-05-09

213- 214:

5月9日，中兴手机正式发布全新一代中兴Axon 40 Ultra，成为吴京代言之后的首款旗舰产品。作为中兴手机推动屏下摄像技术更新迭代、持续领跑多主摄融合计算摄影先锋技术的集大成之作，中兴Axon 40 Ultra加持全新一代骁龙8旗舰芯片的精准调校，从屏幕、影像、性能“三位一体”打造直板旗舰的终极形态，应运时代“为大场面而生”。

215-

216-

中兴通讯高级副总裁、终端事业部总裁倪飞表示：“中兴手机在科技创新的道路上，始终保持着年轻的斗志和对创新的渴望。Axon也曾以多个全球第一，为行业开辟一条条新赛道。作为一款极具想象力的全新旗舰产品，中兴Axon 40 Ultra不仅拥有炫酷的黑科技，还做到了艺术与科技兼备，助力用户驾驭每个‘大场面’，真正为勇敢者助力，与勇敢者同行。”

217-

218:

全新一代柔性屏下摄像技术 每一眼皆是大场面

219:

作为屏下摄像技术先锋，中兴手机从行业首创到自我革新，始终引领全面屏发展趋势。站在连续两代产品全球领先首发的基础上，中兴Axon 40 Ultra再以全新一代柔性屏下摄像技术，实现商用第三代产品的创新突破，用全然一体的无缺屏幕形态，带来全面屏的终极呈现。

220:

新机屏下摄像区屏幕采用400PPI高像素密度，全屏蓝钻排列，视觉融合效果更加完美；业界首发独立像素一驱一技术，每个像素单元都由单独的像素电路驱动，屏幕显示更清晰精细。电路采用分布式透明走线，消除屏下区边缘电路聚集，画面呈现更平滑自然。UDC Pro屏显芯片进一步升级，融合MRC算法升级和智能像素增强、智能显示优化技术，令显示更为精准、同步。凭借全新100%无缺全面屏，中兴Axon 40 Ultra带来更完美的沉浸式观感，每一眼皆为大场面。

221-

222:

前摄影像升级与全面屏进阶同步。中兴Axon 40 Ultra配备1600万像素前置屏下摄像头，可达2.24μm融合大像素效果，为屏下摄像区带来更大感光量。前摄灵透算法3.0通过AI深度学习降噪，可在不同光线环境进行画面实时校准，智能去雾化、智能抗炫光，大幅提升成像清晰度和通透度。智能美颜还可进一步提升面部拍摄效果。

223-

224-

旗舰级屏幕配置更添无穷精彩。新机配备6.8英寸AMOLED大屏，支持1116*2480分辨率FHD+，峰值亮度可达1500nit，100%覆盖DCI-P3广色域，10bit色深，10.7亿色显示，带来极致色彩和清晰度；支持120Hz智能高刷新率、360Hz触控采样率。1440Hz高频PWM调光功能可有效降低昏暗场景的屏幕闪烁度，加上德国莱茵TUV低蓝光护眼认证，高规格呵护双眼健康。

225-

226-

定制光学三主摄计算摄影 每一刻皆为大场面

227:

What you need to know about the ZTE Axon 40 Ultra

54:

The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is a flagship-level smartphone that’s the top-end device in ZTE’s portfolio for 2022 so far. It’s a successor in some ways to last year’s Axon 30 Ultra, offering a brand-new flagship SoC and a bigger battery. But it also steps back in a couple of ways, with a shorter range zoom camera and dropping ever so slightly from a 144Hz display to 120Hz.

Otherwise, you’re getting some premium specs, such as the much-hyped under-display selfie camera, a triple 64MP rear camera system, and a 5,000mAh battery with 65W wired charging.

ZTE’s smartphone launched in China in May 2022 before a global launch on June 8 with general availability from June 21. These global markets include Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, North America, and South Africa. It comes in Black (pictured), Gold, or Silver colorways.

ZTE also launched the $499 Axon 40 Pro globally, which is a step below the Ultra model. It differs by virtue of its Snapdragon 870 chipset, 100MP main camera (along with 8MP+2MP+2MP sensors), and a 144Hz OLED screen. It also lacks the under-display selfie camera seen on the Ultra device.

55:

What’s good?

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

The Axon 40 Ultra sports a premium, if quite slippery, design featuring a brushed glass back and a sizeable camera bump. The former means fingerprints aren’t a concern at all, although the latter does make for plenty of wobbling when flat on a table. I also somehow scuffed the glass back during testing, which isn’t a great sign considering I didn’t drop it. Regardless, you’ll want to slap on the included TPU case or buy another case as it’s quite slippery in the hand.

56:
The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra looks like a premium offering, while the under-display selfie camera makes for an uninterrupted screen.

The most striking design choice is the lack of a punch-hole selfie cutout, pop-up camera module, or notch. That’s right; you’ve got an uninterrupted display here thanks to the in-display selfie camera. I found that the camera wasn’t visible most of the time, though you’ll notice a very slight smudge every now and again whenever the screen shows gray shades and blurred backgrounds. You can also see the sensor itself if you specifically look for it in direct sunlight, but it mostly melts into the background and doesn’t present any haziness on the display. It’s certainly a big step up from the obvious under-display camera blob on the Galaxy Z Fold 3.

Dive under the hood and you’ll find the Axon 40 Ultra’s core specs can rival the very best thanks to the Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 SoC, 8GB to 12GB of RAM, and 128GB or 256GB of storage. Benchmark results show both the 3DMark Wild Life and Geekbench 5 three-run average scores were on the lower end of the Gen 1’s performance charts, but still will within expectation for an elite Android flagship.

Fortunately, the Axon 40 Ultra generally holds up well when it comes to real-world usage. Flicking through home screens, launching apps, and scrolling was a fluid experience, while performance during camera usage was mostly smooth bar a few software gremlins (more on that later). The Axon 40 Ultra deftly handled demanding games like Call of Duty Mobile, Genshin Impact, and Apex Legends. You’re not going to get a buttery smooth experience in Genshin Impact by turning everything to maximum, but that’s par for the course for all Android flagships anyway.

There isn’t a ton of bloatware on the phone, and what is present — a generic Browser app, Booking.com, and Facebook — can be removed. There’s also a ZTE Cares support app and a file manager. Otherwise, first-party apps are otherwise eschewed in favor of Google-backed options. That means Google Photos, YouTube Music, Gmail, and other Google apps instead of redundant OEM equivalents.

57-
The Axon 40 Ultra has the performance and battery longevity of a top Android flagship.

The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is equipped with a 5,000mAh battery and it indeed delivers a healthy level of endurance, with an average of over seven hours of screen-on time in our testing. Even with heavy use — several hours of GPS navigation, an hour of YouTube, and some games — and with the automatic refresh rate option enabled, the phone didn’t stop going until about 10 AM the next day. I was also able to get about eight and a half hours of screen-on time with light usage over two days (YouTube, Telegram, only a few minutes of gaming).

58-
59:

Once the battery hits zero, you can take advantage of 65W wired charging support. Best of all, this charger is included in the box and supports USB PD PPS for charging your other gadgets too. The Axon 40 Ultra took just 41 minutes to go from zero to 100% capacity, hitting 63% after 20 minutes.

The Axon 40 Ultra is also packing a 6.8-inch 120Hz FHD+ OLED screen that isn’t quite cutting-edge anymore but still delivers a pleasant viewing experience. I had no problem using the device in direct sunlight, while colors seemed accurate to the eye and the temperature leaned on the warmer side. You can also tune the colors with a three-stage slider (colorful, standard, soft) and adjust the temperature using a three-stage slider or a more granular tool.

60:

What’s not so good?

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

There are a few areas where ZTE could’ve delivered more polish, with the under-display selfie camera perhaps being the biggest problem. Simply put, this hidden 16MP shooter might be innovative, but as an actual front-facing camera, it can’t hold a candle to mid-range phones and older flagships, let alone recent high-end phones.

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
A portrait selfie.
61:

Even pictures taken in ideal conditions can see smeared hair and plenty of noise, along with a vaseline effect that’s only more pronounced in indoor and backlit scenes. Portrait selfies are also raw, let alone half-baked. ZTE is resorting to beautification by default, presumably to draw attention away from the obvious cutout errors and smeared look.

It really says a lot about the state of under-display cameras that ZTE is on its third generation of the tech and images still look worse than many budget phones, despite the brand’s claims that image quality is “vastly improved.” Check out the next section for our thoughts on the rest of the Axon 40 Ultra’s cameras.

62:

Related: The best selfie camera phones

63-
64:

Software can make or break powerful hardware, but it must be said that ZTE’s My OS isn’t the most memorable Android skin by any measure. It looks and feels like stock Android in several areas (no bad thing), although the default color scheme recalls Apple’s iOS. Fortunately, you can customize things such as the notification shade colors and icon shapes. Ultimately though, it doesn’t have as many features as the likes of One UI and MIUI.

The biggest software disappointment, however, is the apparent lack of an extended update pledge. We’ve seen the likes of Google and Samsung up the ante with up to five years of security patches, but ZTE hasn’t gone on record about long-term support for its latest flagship. In fact, it only said that the Axon 30 series and higher (therefore including the Axon 40 Ultra) would receive security patches every three months. That’s very disappointing for a flagship phone.

While the Axon 40 Ultra has a generally good screen, it’s not the best out there. The most notable issue is that it isn’t a battery-efficient LTPO panel like similarly-priced rivals, and the refresh rate only switches between 60Hz and 120Hz in adaptive mode. This is also a curved screen and I found the touch rejection to be too aggressive, sometimes requiring a longer, more deliberate upward swipe to close an app on the edge of the recents menu.

65:
The Axon 40 Ultra misses out on a few premium extras that rival devices have.

ZTE’s phone won’t win any awards for its dual stereo speakers either, as most of the volume comes from the bottom-firing unit. That means accidentally covering up this speaker will leave you with super soft audio. By comparison, phones like the POCO F4 GT offer quad stereo speakers with well-balanced audio at a much cheaper price. Nevertheless, the Axon 40 Ultra’s speakers are certainly loud enough for podcasts while working in the kitchen.

It also lacks the polish of the very best Android phones on the market. The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra in-display fingerprint sensor is another aspect that left us wanting, offering a few more reading errors and being a little bit slower compared to other phones with in-display scanners. Additionally, ZTE’s latest flagship doesn’t support wireless charging or have an IP rating, two things you would fairly take for granted at this price point. Furthermore, the display glass and the rear glass are only Gorilla Glass 5. Corning is several generations ahead at this point and most Android flagships opt for Victus, or at the very least Gorilla Glass 6. This might not be the most durable flagship out there.

66:

ZTE Axon 40 Ultra camera review

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

Out and about and want to take some snaps? Then you’ll be glad to know that the Axon 40 Ultra’s 64MP (35mm equivalent) main camera does an excellent job during the day. The dynamic range isn’t nearly as wide as some of the best camera phones but it’s still solid. Colors fall on the realistic side, and reliable focusing means consistently sharp images. It doesn’t hurt that the camera app usually delivers clean images that don’t go overboard with the sharpening.

67-
68:

The ultrawide lens is capable of some eye-pleasing, detailed results during the day as well, using the same IMX787 sensor as the main camera. However, colors are noticeably inconsistent between the two cameras, noise is easy to spot in the shadows, and it’s not uncommon to find mushiness at the edge of pictures. At least this camera has autofocus, allowing it to take some sharp macro mode shots.

69-
70:

When night comes, you’ll find that neither the primary camera nor the ultrawide sensor can hang with the best of them. You’ll notice plenty of noise and a dark image when the sun goes down, with the ultrawide being much worse off. Thankfully, the night mode is a truly transformative affair here, clawing back noise, increasing the brightness, and retaining some detail to deliver some good images. Low-light snaps taken with the ultrawide camera are also very soft, but the night mode helps here too.

71-
72:

The third camera here is a 64MP periscope lens, and it’s only equivalent to ~2.6x zoom (or 3.5x compared to more conventional primary cameras). The color profile predictably doesn’t line up with the main camera, but it nevertheless delivers a good level of detail and offers usable images up to about 4x or 5x. Any longer-range zoom is a no-go due to blown-out highlights, blurry edges, and a watercolor effect.

Video quality is pretty solid here too, featuring punchy colors and generally effective stabilization. However, I did notice a fair amount of frame-rate judder now and again in both 4K/60fps and 8K modes. The lack of a dedicated super steady mode is also lamentable here when other brands all offer this option. There are a wide variety of video quality options though, including 8K, 4K/60fps, 4K/120fps, 1080p/240fps, and 720p/480fps.

73:
The Axon 40 Ultra's main camera takes some great shots during the day, and there are loads of interesting modes on offer.

Speaking of variety, those who value a smorgasbord of modes will like what they see here, as the Axon 40 Ultra’s camera app comes with plenty to choose from. Aside from the expected pro/manual, night, portrait, macro, and timelapse options, you’ve also got a vlog option, full-resolution mode, document scanner, and the aforementioned slow-mo options. You’ve also got an electronic shutter option (basically a bokeh mode), multi-exposure mode (overlaying two exposures in one image), a clone mode, Hitchcock zoom option, drama shot-style trajectory mode, a few light painting options, and a starry sky mode for astrophotography. The latter includes options like constellation overlays using augmented reality, which is something I haven’t seen in an OEM camera app before.

One of my favorite modes has to be the multi-camera option though, allowing you to take shots from all three rear cameras at once. It’s not perfect, as the zoom lens often has focusing issues, but it’s still a swell time-saver. You can also place a different camera in the primary viewfinder, so if you want the telephoto lens in the primary viewfinder and the ultrawide and 1x camera in the smaller windows, you can do that too.

74:
75:

While we appreciate the number of camera features on board here, the camera app does need some polishing. For example, we encountered some freezing in the viewfinder when wanting to review the most recently taken photos. We also found that the camera app crashed without fail when switching to the video option and then choosing the tele lens. Zoom controls aren’t always consistent, either. Shooting with the standard mode gives you zoom controls just above the camera mode carousel (e.g. a “1x” icon flanked by icons for wide and tele cameras), but switching to the Night and Pro modes sees separate zoom controls placed on the left-hand side (when held in portrait). The “1x” icon is still above the camera mode carousel, but you can’t actually tap it to switch between cameras — check out the last image in the gallery above.

76:
The Axon 40 Ultra camera app has loads of features, but it needs an overhauled design and more polish.

It’s also possible to record videos from multiple cameras at once, and it’s a feature we’ve wanted to see on more phones since Xiaomi did it with the Mi 11 Ultra. Unfortunately, it looks like the Axon 40 Ultra’s mode needs improving too. We don’t mind that the quality is limited to 1080p/30fps (or 24fps at times), but what’s the point of sacrificing resolution when the frame rate is extremely choppy?

It also doesn’t help that the camera UI feels like it hasn’t been updated since 2014. ZTE could easily roll some of the more experimental features (like the three light painting modes) into one, and more generally could make much better use of the viewfinder to host frequently used settings for quick access.

ZTE Axon 40 Ultra review: The verdict

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

The Axon 40 Ultra gets most of the basics right, delivering a high-powered, long-lasting smartphone that tops up in under an hour. The addition of versatile rear cameras and that full-screen experience enabled by a stealthy under-display selfie camera means you’ve got an intriguing yet capable proposition at a very reasonable asking price.

However, it’s clear that there are a few gaps in the Axon 40 Ultra’s armor, starting with those disappointing selfies. Even at a more affordable flagship price, just shy of $800 is a tough ask for a phone that lacks an IP rating, wireless charging, and a long-term update pledge. There are a few alternatives on the market that come in at the same price or undercut the ZTE device while offering these extras.

79:
The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is a powerful, long-lasting, fast-charging phone at an affordable price, but it lacks some flagship polish.

Speaking of alternatives, we’d definitely recommend you look at the Google Pixel 6 ($599). For $200 less, you can get a relatively powerful smartphone with great image quality, a long commitment to updates, Pixel-exclusive software features, a relatively large battery, and that IP68/wireless charging combo. It lacks the beefy Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 chipset, telephoto camera, and fast charging though. Meanwhile, for an extra $100, the Google Pixel 6 Pro ($899) adds that missing zoom camera, ups the display refresh rate and resolution, and packs an even larger battery.

The Samsung Galaxy S22 ($799) is another alternative worth investigating, and it’s probably the most widely available alternative on the list. It packs the same chipset, an extended update pledge, more software features, an IP68 rating, and wireless charging. You do miss out on fast charging and that 3,700mAh battery has us concerned about how it’ll hold up over time.

80:

Check out: The best phone deals

The OnePlus 10 Pro ($899) might be another device you should consider in lieu of the Axon 40 Ultra. It doesn’t have an under-display selfie camera and costs $100 more, but you’re getting perks like wireless charging, a good primary camera, a superior screen, and three years of OS updates. It also shares a few of the Axon 40 Ultra’s strengths such as battery life, fast charging, and the same powerful processor, though it’s a little rough around the edges due to the similarly lacking IP rating (unless you buy from T-Mobile), mediocre supporting cameras, and some software inconsistencies.

You should also keep the iPhone 13 ($799) in mind if you’re open to joining the Apple ecosystem. It lacks a high refresh rate screen, has a massive notch, lacks a telephoto camera, and misses out on fast charging (and the charger). However, Apple’s phone also brings a powerful processor, IP68 rating, wireless charging, and access to an exclusive ecosystem.

26-为大场面而生 终极直板旗舰中兴Axon 40 Ultra正式发布
27-2022-05-09
28:5月9日，中兴手机正式发布全新一代中兴Axon 40 Ultra，成为吴京代言之后的首款旗舰产品。作为中兴手机推动屏下摄像技术更新迭代、持续领跑多主摄融合计算摄影先锋技术的集大成之作，中兴Axon 40 Ultra加持全新一代骁龙8旗舰芯片的精准调校，从屏幕、影像、性能“三位一体”打造直板旗舰的终极形态，应运时代“为大场面而生”。
29-中兴通讯高级副总裁、终端事业部总裁倪飞表示：“中兴手机在科技创新的道路上，始终保持着年轻的斗志和对创新的渴望。Axon也曾以多个全球第一，为行业开辟一条条新赛道。作为一款极具想象力的全新旗舰产品，中兴Axon 40 Ultra不仅拥有炫酷的黑科技，还做到了艺术与科技兼备，助力用户驾驭每个‘大场面’，真正为勇敢者助力，与勇敢者同行。”
30:全新一代柔性屏下摄像技术 每一眼皆是大场面
31:作为屏下摄像技术先锋，中兴手机从行业首创到自我革新，始终引领全面屏发展趋势。站在连续两代产品全球领先首发的基础上，中兴Axon 40 Ultra再以全新一代柔性屏下摄像技术，实现商用第三代产品的创新突破，用全然一体的无缺屏幕形态，带来全面屏的终极呈现。
32:新机屏下摄像区屏幕采用400PPI高像素密度，全屏蓝钻排列，视觉融合效果更加完美；业界首发独立像素一驱一技术，每个像素单元都由单独的像素电路驱动，屏幕显示更清晰精细。电路采用分布式透明走线，消除屏下区边缘电路聚集，画面呈现更平滑自然。UDC Pro屏显芯片进一步升级，融合MRC算法升级和智能像素增强、智能显示优化技术，令显示更为精准、同步。凭借全新100%无缺全面屏，中兴Axon 40 Ultra带来更完美的沉浸式观感，每一眼皆为大场面。
33:前摄影像升级与全面屏进阶同步。中兴Axon 40 Ultra配备1600万像素前置屏下摄像头，可达2.24μm融合大像素效果，为屏下摄像区带来更大感光量。前摄灵透算法3.0通过AI深度学习降噪，可在不同光线环境进行画面实时校准，智能去雾化、智能抗炫光，大幅提升成像清晰度和通透度。智能美颜还可进一步提升面部拍摄效果。
34-旗舰级屏幕配置更添无穷精彩。新机配备6.8英寸AMOLED大屏，支持1116*2480分辨率FHD+，峰值亮度可达1500nit，100%覆盖DCI-P3广色域，10bit色深，10.7亿色显示，带来极致色彩和清晰度；支持120Hz智能高刷新率、360Hz触控采样率。1440Hz高频PWM调光功能可有效降低昏暗场景的屏幕闪烁度，加上德国莱茵TUV低蓝光护眼认证，高规格呵护双眼健康。
35-定制光学三主摄计算摄影 每一刻皆为大场面
36:在全面屏让用户“看见大场面”的同时，中兴Axon 40 Ultra三主摄配置全面升级，打造涵盖6400万像素超人文主摄、6400万像素超广角主摄、6400万像素潜望式长焦主摄的业界最强三主摄，匹配多个“业界唯一”的强大计算影像能力，进一步成就“记录大场面”的影像旗舰。
37:新机人文和广角主摄行业首发双索尼IMX787传感器，可实现双全像素全向对焦，对焦更为快速精准。其中人文主摄采用35mm等效焦距，搭载7P镜头，匹配f/1.6大光圈，具备硬件级光学虚化效果。广角主摄采用16mm等效焦距，4cm AF微距，广角微距二合一，自由曲面超低畸变。长焦主摄采用91mm等效焦距。从广角到长焦可实现5.7倍的光学变焦。搭载斯坦尼康级全系统防抖，双OIS光学防抖+ EIS防抖让每一张大片都能“稳”操胜券。
38:计算影像再升级。中兴Axon 40 Ultra作为业界同像素三主摄手机中，唯一主摄全部支持8k超高清录影的产品，可以更全面的视角将万千细节尽收其中；也是业界唯一三主摄均配备闪电抓拍功能，可通过定制自适应快门影追算法实现运动主体的快速、清晰抓拍；同时也是业界唯一三主摄全部采用预设对焦，能在拍摄前手动预设对焦距离，进一步减少对焦时间。
39-超级夜景视频功能进一步增强，独有的AI视频超画质算法可提升画面亮度、增强暗区的解析力、动态范围、降低噪声，真实还原色彩信息。智慧月亮、星空增强、AI星座等星空摄影玩法，人文影像色彩系统，以及布列松大师黑白滤镜、胶片滤镜等丰富的人文滤镜，更助力用户玩转多种影像场景。
40-硬核性能与大气美学兼修 每一秒无惧大场面
41-为大场面而生，还需要无惧性能挑战，和天生自带气场，掌控每一个大场面。中兴Axon 40 Ultra搭载全新骁龙8+UFS3.1+满血LPDDR5旗舰配置。九层散热架构散热总面积可达36356mm
--
44-为释放游戏影音性能，中兴Axon 40 Ultra还配备Snapdragon Sound及DTS音效立体双扬声器、X轴线性马达、90/120高帧率，体验全面震撼升级。车道级高精度导航支持L1+L5双频定位，可精准识别当前所在车道。此外，新机还搭载红外遥控，配备强大的红外码库，支持拍照识别遥控器，快速完成配对。提供5000mAh电池和80W超级快充、独立安全芯片，支持硬件加密，强势护航系统安全。
45-外观方面，中兴Axon 40 Ultra自然天成的一体化设计，彰显天生大气。新机采用71度超大弧度“瀑布式”曲面设计，3.9mm超深弯折度握持更贴合手感。背部采用业界首创的后摄无边框玻璃设计，将金属平台面完美“隐藏”。Label设计2.0更加简洁纯粹。配色拥有水墨、敦煌两种国风高级感配色可选。
46-硬核双旗舰同时发布 满足多元期待
47:此次发布会还带来了中兴Axon 40 Pro及终端生态产品。中兴Axon 40 Pro配备AI四摄，拥有1亿像素主摄，支持闪电抓拍功能及人文影像色彩系统，可进行4K视频录制；搭载6.67英寸FHD+ AMOLED 柔性曲面屏，144Hz刷新率；采用高通骁龙870，66W闪电快充及5000mAh电池。新机提供幻夜黑、晶雾蓝、星光橙三种配色可选。
48-中兴AX3000巡天版路由采用自研双核心主芯片，支持160MHz宽频，满血WiFi6，覆盖面积可达120平方米，且支持一键组网和游戏加速器。小兴看看守护神云台则采用2.5K分辨率，支持微光全彩和超清红外夜视，超广角覆盖，配合AI智能监测，可实现24小时全天候高清监控。
49-即日起，中兴Axon 40 Ultra将在中兴商城、京东、天猫、苏宁等平台开启预售/预约，并于5月13日全渠道正式开售，8GB+ 256G版售价4998元，12G+256G版售价5298元，12G +512G版售价5798元，16G + 1T版售价7298元。中兴Axon 40 Pro 8G + 256G版售价2998元，12G+ 256G版售价3298元，12G+ 512G版售价3798元。中兴AX3000巡天版路由器售价289元，小兴看看守护神云台2.5K版售价229元。

81-The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is a flagship-level smartphone that’s the top-end device in ZTE’s portfolio for 2022 so far. It’s a successor in some ways to last year’s
82-Axon 30 Ultra
83:, offering a brand-new flagship SoC and a bigger battery. But it also steps back in a couple of ways, with a shorter range zoom camera and dropping ever so slightly from a 144Hz display to 120Hz.
84:Otherwise, you’re getting some premium specs, such as the much-hyped under-display selfie camera, a triple 64MP rear camera system, and a 5,000mAh battery with 65W wired charging.
85-ZTE’s smartphone launched in China in May 2022 before a global launch on June 8 with general availability from June 21. These global markets include Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, North America, and South Africa. It comes in Black (pictured), Gold, or Silver colorways.
86:ZTE also launched the $499 Axon 40 Pro globally, which is a step below the Ultra model. It differs by virtue of its Snapdragon 870 chipset, 100MP main camera (along with 8MP+2MP+2MP sensors), and a 144Hz OLED screen. It also lacks the under-display selfie camera seen on the Ultra device.
87-What’s good?
88-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
89-The Axon 40 Ultra sports a premium, if quite slippery, design featuring a brushed glass back and a sizeable camera bump. The former means fingerprints aren’t a concern at all, although the latter does make for plenty of wobbling when flat on a table. I also somehow scuffed the glass back during testing, which isn’t a great sign considering I didn’t drop it. Regardless, you’ll want to slap on the included TPU case or buy another case as it’s quite slippery in the hand.
90:The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra looks like a premium offering, while the under-display selfie camera makes for an uninterrupted screen.
91:The most striking design choice is the lack of a punch-hole selfie cutout, pop-up camera module, or notch. That’s right; you’ve got an uninterrupted display here thanks to the in-display selfie camera. I found that the camera wasn’t visible most of the time, though you’ll notice a very slight smudge every now and again whenever the screen shows gray shades and blurred backgrounds. You can also see the sensor itself if you specifically look for it in direct sunlight, but it mostly melts into the background and doesn’t present any haziness on the display. It’s certainly a big step up from the obvious under-display camera blob on the
92-Galaxy Z Fold 3
93-.
94-Dive under the hood and you’ll find the Axon 40 Ultra’s core specs can rival the very best thanks to the
95-Snapdragon 8 Gen 1
96-SoC, 8GB to 12GB of RAM, and 128GB or 256GB of storage. Benchmark results show both the 3DMark Wild Life and Geekbench 5 three-run average scores were on the lower end of the Gen 1’s performance charts, but still will within expectation for an elite Android flagship.
97:Fortunately, the Axon 40 Ultra generally holds up well when it comes to real-world usage. Flicking through home screens, launching apps, and scrolling was a fluid experience, while performance during camera usage was mostly smooth bar a few software gremlins (more on that later). The Axon 40 Ultra deftly handled demanding games like Call of Duty Mobile, Genshin Impact, and Apex Legends. You’re not going to get a buttery smooth experience in Genshin Impact by turning everything to maximum, but that’s par for the course for all Android flagships anyway.
98-There isn’t a ton of bloatware on the phone, and what is present — a generic Browser app, Booking.com, and Facebook — can be removed. There’s also a ZTE Cares support app and a file manager. Otherwise, first-party apps are otherwise eschewed in favor of Google-backed options. That means Google Photos, YouTube Music, Gmail, and other Google apps instead of redundant OEM equivalents.
99-The Axon 40 Ultra has the performance and battery longevity of a top Android flagship.
100-The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is equipped with a 5,000mAh battery and it indeed delivers a healthy level of endurance, with an average of over seven hours of screen-on time in our testing. Even with heavy use — several hours of GPS navigation, an hour of YouTube, and some games — and with the automatic refresh rate option enabled, the phone didn’t stop going until about 10 AM the next day. I was also able to get about eight and a half hours of screen-on time with light usage over two days (YouTube, Telegram, only a few minutes of gaming).
101-Once the battery hits zero, you can take advantage of 65W wired charging support. Best of all, this charger is included in the box and supports

123:The Axon 40 Ultra is also packing a 6.8-inch 120Hz FHD+ OLED screen that isn’t quite cutting-edge anymore but still delivers a pleasant viewing experience. I had no problem using the device in direct sunlight, while colors seemed accurate to the eye and the temperature leaned on the warmer side. You can also tune the colors with a three-stage slider (colorful, standard, soft) and adjust the temperature using a three-stage slider or a more granular tool.
124-What’s not so good?
125-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
126:There are a few areas where ZTE could’ve delivered more polish, with the under-display selfie camera perhaps being the biggest problem. Simply put, this hidden 16MP shooter might be innovative, but as an actual front-facing camera, it can’t hold a candle to mid-range phones and older flagships, let alone recent high-end phones.
127-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
128:A portrait selfie.
129:A selfie shot outdoors.

132:Even pictures taken in ideal conditions can see smeared hair and plenty of noise, along with a vaseline effect that’s only more pronounced in indoor and backlit scenes. Portrait selfies are also raw, let alone half-baked. ZTE is resorting to beautification by default, presumably to draw attention away from the obvious cutout errors and smeared look.
133:It really says a lot about the state of under-display cameras that ZTE is on its third generation of the tech and images still look worse than many budget phones, despite the brand’s claims that image quality is “vastly improved.” Check out the next section for our thoughts on the rest of the Axon 40 Ultra’s cameras.
134-Related:
135:The best selfie camera phones
136:Software can make or break powerful hardware, but it must be said that ZTE’s My OS isn’t the most memorable Android skin by any measure. It looks and feels like
137-stock Android
138-in several areas (no bad thing), although the default color scheme recalls Apple’s iOS. Fortunately, you can customize things such as the notification shade colors and icon shapes. Ultimately though, it doesn’t have as many features as the likes of One UI and MIUI.
139:The biggest software disappointment, however, is the apparent lack of an extended update pledge. We’ve seen the likes of Google and Samsung up the ante with up to five years of security patches, but ZTE hasn’t gone on record about long-term support for its latest flagship. In fact, it only said that the Axon 30 series and higher (therefore including the Axon 40 Ultra) would receive security patches every three months. That’s very disappointing for a flagship phone.
140-While the Axon 40 Ultra has a generally good screen, it’s not the best out there. The most notable issue is that it isn’t a battery-efficient
141-LTPO
142-panel like similarly-priced rivals, and the refresh rate only switches between 60Hz and 120Hz in adaptive mode. This is also a curved screen and I found the touch rejection to be too aggressive, sometimes requiring a longer, more deliberate upward swipe to close an app on the edge of the recents menu.
143-The Axon 40 Ultra misses out on a few premium extras that rival devices have.
144:ZTE’s phone won’t win any awards for its dual stereo speakers either, as most of the volume comes from the bottom-firing unit. That means accidentally covering up this speaker will leave you with super soft audio. By comparison, phones like the
145-POCO F4 GT
146-offer quad stereo speakers with well-balanced audio at a much cheaper price. Nevertheless, the Axon 40 Ultra’s speakers are certainly loud enough for podcasts while working in the kitchen.
147:It also lacks the polish of the very best Android phones on the market. The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra in-display fingerprint sensor is another aspect that left us wanting, offering a few more reading errors and being a little bit slower compared to other phones with in-display scanners. Additionally, ZTE’s latest flagship doesn’t support wireless charging or have an IP rating, two things you would fairly take for granted at this price point. Furthermore, the display glass and the rear glass are only Gorilla Glass 5. Corning is several generations ahead at this point and most Android flagships opt for Victus, or at the very least Gorilla Glass 6. This might not be the most durable flagship out there.
148-ZTE Axon 40 Ultra camera review
149-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
150-Out and about and want to take some snaps? Then you’ll be glad to know that the Axon 40 Ultra’s 64MP (35mm equivalent) main camera does an excellent job during the day. The dynamic range isn’t nearly as wide as some of the
151-best camera phones
--

158-The
159-ultrawide lens
160:is capable of some eye-pleasing, detailed results during the day as well, using the same IMX787 sensor as the main camera. However, colors are noticeably inconsistent between the two cameras, noise is easy to spot in the shadows, and it’s not uncommon to find mushiness at the edge of pictures. At least this camera has autofocus, allowing it to take some sharp macro mode shots.
161-1x
162-Night mode
163-1x
164-Night mode
165:When night comes, you’ll find that neither the primary camera nor the ultrawide sensor can hang with the best of them. You’ll notice plenty of noise and a dark image when the sun goes down, with the ultrawide being much worse off. Thankfully, the night mode is a truly transformative affair here, clawing back noise, increasing the brightness, and retaining some detail to deliver some good images. Low-light snaps taken with the ultrawide camera are also very soft, but the night mode helps here too.
166-Ultrawide
167-1x
168-5x
169:The third camera here is a 64MP periscope lens, and it’s only equivalent to ~2.6x zoom (or 3.5x compared to more conventional primary cameras). The color profile predictably doesn’t line up with the main camera, but it nevertheless delivers a good level of detail and offers usable images up to about 4x or 5x. Any longer-range zoom is a no-go due to blown-out highlights, blurry edges, and a watercolor effect.
170-Video quality is pretty solid here too, featuring punchy colors and generally effective stabilization. However, I did notice a fair amount of frame-rate judder now and again in both 4K/60fps and 8K modes. The lack of a dedicated super steady mode is also lamentable here when other brands all offer this option. There are a wide variety of video quality options though, including 8K, 4K/60fps, 4K/120fps, 1080p/240fps, and 720p/480fps.
171-The Axon 40 Ultra's main camera takes some great shots during the day, and there are loads of interesting modes on offer.
172-Speaking of variety, those who value a smorgasbord of modes will like what they see here, as the Axon 40 Ultra’s camera app comes with plenty to choose from. Aside from the expected pro/manual, night, portrait, macro, and timelapse options, you’ve also got a vlog option, full-resolution mode, document scanner, and the aforementioned slow-mo options. You’ve also got an electronic shutter option (basically a bokeh mode), multi-exposure mode (overlaying two exposures in one image), a clone mode, Hitchcock zoom option, drama shot-style trajectory mode, a few light painting options, and a starry sky mode for astrophotography. The latter includes options like constellation overlays using augmented reality, which is something I haven’t seen in an OEM camera app before.
173-One of my favorite modes has to be the multi-camera option though, allowing you to take shots from all three rear cameras at once. It’s not perfect, as the zoom lens often has focusing issues, but it’s still a swell time-saver. You can also place a different camera in the primary viewfinder, so if you want the telephoto lens in the primary viewfinder and the ultrawide and 1x camera in the smaller windows, you can do that too.
--
178-. Unfortunately, it looks like the Axon 40 Ultra’s mode needs improving too. We don’t mind that the quality is limited to 1080p/30fps (or 24fps at times), but what’s the point of sacrificing resolution when the frame rate is extremely choppy?
179-It also doesn’t help that the camera UI feels like it hasn’t been updated since 2014. ZTE could easily roll some of the more experimental features (like the three light painting modes) into one, and more generally could make much better use of the viewfinder to host frequently used settings for quick access.

81-The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is a flagship-level smartphone that’s the top-end device in ZTE’s portfolio for 2022 so far. It’s a successor in some ways to last year’s
82-Axon 30 Ultra
83-, offering a brand-new flagship SoC and a bigger battery. But it also steps back in a couple of ways, with a shorter range zoom camera and dropping ever so slightly from a 144Hz display to 120Hz.
84:Otherwise, you’re getting some premium specs, such as the much-hyped under-display selfie camera, a triple 64MP rear camera system, and a 5,000mAh battery with 65W wired charging.
85-ZTE’s smartphone launched in China in May 2022 before a global launch on June 8 with general availability from June 21. These global markets include Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, North America, and South Africa. It comes in Black (pictured), Gold, or Silver colorways.
86:ZTE also launched the $499 Axon 40 Pro globally, which is a step below the Ultra model. It differs by virtue of its Snapdragon 870 chipset, 100MP main camera (along with 8MP+2MP+2MP sensors), and a 144Hz OLED screen. It also lacks the under-display selfie camera seen on the Ultra device.
87-What’s good?
88-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
89-The Axon 40 Ultra sports a premium, if quite slippery, design featuring a brushed glass back and a sizeable camera bump. The former means fingerprints aren’t a concern at all, although the latter does make for plenty of wobbling when flat on a table. I also somehow scuffed the glass back during testing, which isn’t a great sign considering I didn’t drop it. Regardless, you’ll want to slap on the included TPU case or buy another case as it’s quite slippery in the hand.
90:The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra looks like a premium offering, while the under-display selfie camera makes for an uninterrupted screen.
91:The most striking design choice is the lack of a punch-hole selfie cutout, pop-up camera module, or notch. That’s right; you’ve got an uninterrupted display here thanks to the in-display selfie camera. I found that the camera wasn’t visible most of the time, though you’ll notice a very slight smudge every now and again whenever the screen shows gray shades and blurred backgrounds. You can also see the sensor itself if you specifically look for it in direct sunlight, but it mostly melts into the background and doesn’t present any haziness on the display. It’s certainly a big step up from the obvious under-display camera blob on the
92-Galaxy Z Fold 3
93-.
94-Dive under the hood and you’ll find the Axon 40 Ultra’s core specs can rival the very best thanks to the
95-Snapdragon 8 Gen 1
96-SoC, 8GB to 12GB of RAM, and 128GB or 256GB of storage. Benchmark results show both the 3DMark Wild Life and Geekbench 5 three-run average scores were on the lower end of the Gen 1’s performance charts, but still will within expectation for an elite Android flagship.
97:Fortunately, the Axon 40 Ultra generally holds up well when it comes to real-world usage. Flicking through home screens, launching apps, and scrolling was a fluid experience, while performance during camera usage was mostly smooth bar a few software gremlins (more on that later). The Axon 40 Ultra deftly handled demanding games like Call of Duty Mobile, Genshin Impact, and Apex Legends. You’re not going to get a buttery smooth experience in Genshin Impact by turning everything to maximum, but that’s par for the course for all Android flagships anyway.
98-There isn’t a ton of bloatware on the phone, and what is present — a generic Browser app, Booking.com, and Facebook — can be removed. There’s also a ZTE Cares support app and a file manager. Otherwise, first-party apps are otherwise eschewed in favor of Google-backed options. That means Google Photos, YouTube Music, Gmail, and other Google apps instead of redundant OEM equivalents.
99-The Axon 40 Ultra has the performance and battery longevity of a top Android flagship.
100-The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is equipped with a 5,000mAh battery and it indeed delivers a healthy level of endurance, with an average of over seven hours of screen-on time in our testing. Even with heavy use — several hours of GPS navigation, an hour of YouTube, and some games — and with the automatic refresh rate option enabled, the phone didn’t stop going until about 10 AM the next day. I was also able to get about eight and a half hours of screen-on time with light usage over two days (YouTube, Telegram, only a few minutes of gaming).
101-Once the battery hits zero, you can take advantage of 65W wired charging support. Best of all, this charger is included in the box and supports
--
119-INIU Outdoor Rugged Power Bank
120-6% off
121-See price at Amazon
122-Limited Time Deal!
123:The Axon 40 Ultra is also packing a 6.8-inch 120Hz FHD+ OLED screen that isn’t quite cutting-edge anymore but still delivers a pleasant viewing experience. I had no problem using the device in direct sunlight, while colors seemed accurate to the eye and the temperature leaned on the warmer side. You can also tune the colors with a three-stage slider (colorful, standard, soft) and adjust the temperature using a three-stage slider or a more granular tool.
124-What’s not so good?
125-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
126:There are a few areas where ZTE could’ve delivered more polish, with the under-display selfie camera perhaps being the biggest problem. Simply put, this hidden 16MP shooter might be innovative, but as an actual front-facing camera, it can’t hold a candle to mid-range phones and older flagships, let alone recent high-end phones.
127-Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
128:A portrait selfie.
129:A selfie shot outdoors.
130-A self-portrait taken indoors during the day.
131:A low-light image with the front camera.
132:Even pictures taken in ideal conditions can see smeared hair and plenty of noise, along with a vaseline effect that’s only more pronounced in indoor and backlit scenes. Portrait selfies are also raw, let alone half-baked. ZTE is resorting to beautification by default, presumably to draw attention away from the obvious cutout errors and smeared look.
133:It really says a lot about the state of under-display cameras that ZTE is on its third generation of the tech and images still look worse than many budget phones, despite the brand’s claims that image quality is “vastly improved.” Check out the next section for our thoughts on the rest of the Axon 40 Ultra’s cameras.
134-Related:
135:The best selfie camera phones
136:Software can make or break powerful hardware, but it must be said that ZTE’s My OS isn’t the most memorable Android skin by any measure. It looks and feels like
137-stock Android
138-in several areas (no bad thing), although the default color scheme recalls Apple’s iOS. Fortunately, you can customize things such as the notification shade colors and icon shapes. Ultimately though, it doesn’t have as many features as the likes of One UI and MIUI.
139:The biggest software disappointment, however, is the apparent lack of an extended update pledge. We’ve seen the likes of Google and Samsung up the ante with up to five years of security patches, but ZTE hasn’t gone on record about long-term support for its latest flagship. In fact, it only said that the Axon 30 series and higher (therefore including the Axon 40 Ultra) would receive security patches every three months. That’s very disappointing for a flagship phone.
140-While the Axon 40 Ultra has a generally good screen, it’s not the best out there. The most notable issue is that it isn’t a battery-efficient
141-LTPO
142-panel like similarly-priced rivals, and the refresh rate only switches between 60Hz and 120Hz in adaptive mode. This is also a curved screen and I found the touch rejection to be too aggressive, sometimes requiring a longer, more deliberate upward swipe to close an app on the edge of the recents menu.
143-The Axon 40 Ultra misses out on a few premium extras that rival devices have.
144:ZTE’s phone won’t win any awards for its dual stereo speakers either, as most of the volume comes from the bottom-firing unit. That means accidentally covering up this speaker will leave you with super soft audio. By comparison, phones like the
145-POCO F4 GT
146-offer quad stereo speakers with well-balanced audio at a much cheaper price. Nevertheless, the Axon 40 Ultra’s speakers are certainly loud enough for podcasts while working in the kitchen.
147-It also lacks the polish of the very best Android phones on the market. The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra in-display fingerprint sensor is another aspect that left us wanting, offering a few more reading errors and being a little bit slower compared to other phones with in-display scanners. Additionally, ZTE’s latest flagship doesn’t support wireless charging or have an IP rating, two things you would fairly take for granted at this price point. Furthermore, the display glass and the rear glass are only Gorilla Glass 5. Corning is several generations ahead at this point and most Android flagships opt for Victus, or at the very least Gorilla Glass 6. This might not be the most durable flagship out there.

158-The
159-ultrawide lens
160:is capable of some eye-pleasing, detailed results during the day as well, using the same IMX787 sensor as the main camera. However, colors are noticeably inconsistent between the two cameras, noise is easy to spot in the shadows, and it’s not uncommon to find mushiness at the edge of pictures. At least this camera has autofocus, allowing it to take some sharp macro mode shots.
161-1x
162-Night mode
163-1x
164-Night mode
165:When night comes, you’ll find that neither the primary camera nor the ultrawide sensor can hang with the best of them. You’ll notice plenty of noise and a dark image when the sun goes down, with the ultrawide being much worse off. Thankfully, the night mode is a truly transformative affair here, clawing back noise, increasing the brightness, and retaining some detail to deliver some good images. Low-light snaps taken with the ultrawide camera are also very soft, but the night mode helps here too.
166-Ultrawide
167-1x
168-5x
169:The third camera here is a 64MP periscope lens, and it’s only equivalent to ~2.6x zoom (or 3.5x compared to more conventional primary cameras). The color profile predictably doesn’t line up with the main camera, but it nevertheless delivers a good level of detail and offers usable images up to about 4x or 5x. Any longer-range zoom is a no-go due to blown-out highlights, blurry edges, and a watercolor effect.
170-Video quality is pretty solid here too, featuring punchy colors and generally effective stabilization. However, I did notice a fair amount of frame-rate judder now and again in both 4K/60fps and 8K modes. The lack of a dedicated super steady mode is also lamentable here when other brands all offer this option. There are a wide variety of video quality options though, including 8K, 4K/60fps, 4K/120fps, 1080p/240fps, and 720p/480fps.
171-The Axon 40 Ultra's main camera takes some great shots during the day, and there are loads of interesting modes on offer.
172-Speaking of variety, those who value a smorgasbord of modes will like what they see here, as the Axon 40 Ultra’s camera app comes with plenty to choose from. Aside from the expected pro/manual, night, portrait, macro, and timelapse options, you’ve also got a vlog option, full-resolution mode, document scanner, and the aforementioned slow-mo options. You’ve also got an electronic shutter option (basically a bokeh mode), multi-exposure mode (overlaying two exposures in one image), a clone mode, Hitchcock zoom option, drama shot-style trajectory mode, a few light painting options, and a starry sky mode for astrophotography. The latter includes options like constellation overlays using augmented reality, which is something I haven’t seen in an OEM camera app before.
173-One of my favorite modes has to be the multi-camera option though, allowing you to take shots from all three rear cameras at once. It’s not perfect, as the zoom lens often has focusing issues, but it’s still a swell time-saver. You can also place a different camera in the primary viewfinder, so if you want the telephoto lens in the primary viewfinder and the ultrawide and 1x camera in the smaller windows, you can do that too.

The Axon 40 Ultra has the performance and battery longevity of a top Android flagship.
The ZTE Axon 40 Ultra is equipped with a 5,000mAh battery and it indeed delivers a healthy level of endurance, with an average of over seven hours of screen-on time in our testing. Even with heavy use — several hours of GPS navigation, an hour of YouTube, and some games — and with the automatic refresh rate option enabled, the phone didn’t stop going until about 10 AM the next day. I was also able to get about eight and a half hours of screen-on time with light usage over two days (YouTube, Telegram, only a few minutes of gaming).
Once the battery hits zero, you can take advantage of 65W wired charging support. Best of all, this charger is included in the box and supports
USB PD PPS
for charging your other gadgets too. The Axon 40 Ultra took just 41 minutes to go from zero to 100% capacity, hitting 63% after 20 minutes.

The Axon 40 Ultra is also packing a 6.8-inch 120Hz FHD+ OLED screen that isn’t quite cutting-edge anymore but still delivers a pleasant viewing experience. I had no problem using the device in direct sunlight, while colors seemed accurate to the eye and the temperature leaned on the warmer side. You can also tune the colors with a three-stage slider (colorful, standard, soft) and adjust the temperature using a three-stage slider or a more granular tool.
What’s not so good?
Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
There are a few areas where ZTE could’ve delivered more polish, with the under-display selfie camera perhaps being the biggest problem. Simply put, this hidden 16MP shooter might be innovative, but as an actual front-facing camera, it can’t hold a candle to mid-range phones and older flagships, let alone recent high-end phones.
Hadlee Simons / Android Authority
A portrait selfie.
A selfie shot outdoors.
A self-portrait taken indoors during the day.

Even pictures taken in ideal conditions can see smeared hair and plenty of noise, along with a vaseline effect that’s only more pronounced in indoor and backlit scenes. Portrait selfies are also raw, let alone half-baked. ZTE is resorting to beautification by default, presumably to draw attention away from the obvious cutout errors and smeared look.
It really says a lot about the state of under-display cameras that ZTE is on its third generation of the tech and images still look worse than many budget phones, despite the brand’s claims that image quality is “vastly improved.” Check out the next section for our thoughts on the rest of the Axon 40 Ultra’s cameras.
Related:
The best selfie camera phones
Software can make or break powerful hardware, but it must be said that ZTE’s My OS isn’t the most memorable Android skin by any measure. It looks and feels like
stock Android
in several areas (no bad thing), although the default color scheme recalls Apple’s iOS. Fortunately, you can customize things such as the notification shade colors and icon shapes. Ultimately though, it doesn’t have as many features as the likes of One UI and MIUI.
The biggest software disappointment, however, is the apparent lack of an extended update pledge. We’ve seen the likes of Google and Samsung up the ante with up to five years of security patches, but ZTE hasn’t gone on record about long-term support for its latest flagship. In fact, it only said that the Axon 30 series and higher (therefore including the Axon 40 Ultra) would receive security patches every three months. That’s very disappointing for a flagship phone.
While the Axon 40 Ultra has a generally good screen, it’s not the best out there. The most notable issue is that it isn’t a battery-efficient
LTPO
panel like similarly-priced rivals, and the refresh rate only switches between 60Hz and 120Hz in adaptive mode. This is also a curved screen and I found the touch rejection to be too aggressive, sometimes requiring a longer, more deliberate upward swipe to close an app on the edge of the recents menu.
The Axon 40 Ultra misses out on a few premium extras that rival devices have.
